Assumption: this is a management screen for existing API keys; whether secrets can be retrieved after creation is unspecified. Show key name, masked identifier, permissions and status in the table. Prefer one-time secret display at creation; if existing-secret reveal is supported, require an explicit, individually named reveal control and remask on leaving the view. Never place secrets in accessible names, logs or toast text.

Give each Copy button a name such as “Copy key for Build agent” and announce completion without moving focus. Keep Rename separate from a clearly labeled Revoke action. Revoke opens a keyboard-accessible confirmation dialog identifying the key and explaining that dependent clients will lose access. Initially focus Cancel; return focus to the initiating control on cancellation. Do not imply revocation is undoable. After success, focus the remaining row status or next sensible control.

Keep forms, entered values and controls mounted on errors. Associate inline errors with fields and focus an error summary after submission; provide a specific recovery action. Keep success status visible until dismissed or superseded, with a polite announcement. On an ambiguous revoke timeout, reconcile the key’s status before offering another attempt. On narrow screens, stack labeled fields and keep destructive actions distinct; support visible focus, sufficient targets and zoom reflow.
answers.verification: Proposed only: walk through create/copy/rename/revoke, cancellation, server error and ambiguous timeout using keyboard and a screen reader; inspect focus restoration, secret exposure, long names and narrow layouts at zoom. No interface was implemented or action taken.

Recommend a version-specific pagination adapter. Q1 directly states the v3 termination contract: continue using the returned cursor until next_cursor is null. A short page is not that condition, so the existing stop rule has no support in Q1 and risks truncation. Q2 establishes that v2 used page numbers; it does not establish a v2 termination rule. Q3 is a third-party example and cannot override Q1’s explicit v3 contract. These are packet-based conclusions, not observations from requests.

Design an offline compatibility experiment with scripted responses: a short first page with a non-null cursor, a subsequent full page, and a final page with next_cursor=null. Compare the existing integration and the proposed adapter against an exact expected ordered item list and requested cursor sequence. Include an empty final page and a full final page, both with null cursors. As a defensive assumption, also exercise an empty nonterminal page rather than treating emptiness as completion.

Test repeated cursors, missing cursor fields and transient failures. Detect cursor cycles and enforce a page/deadline budget; return an explicit incomplete result instead of silently declaring success. Retry only within that budget without skipping pages. Keep v2 behavior isolated and unresolved until its actual termination contract is supplied. Approve v3 migration only after the fixtures demonstrate complete retrieval and clear failure behavior.
answers.verification: Proposed fixtures only; no requests or experiments were run. Check exact item coverage and cursor forwarding, short/full/empty terminal pages, nonterminal short pages, cycle detection, malformed responses and bounded retry exhaustion. Evidence is limited to Q1, Q2 and Q3.

Assumption: the wrapper creates a new worktree and branch under an explicitly configured workspace root. Provide preview and apply modes with the same stable JSON plan; preview performs read-only inspection and never reserves or creates paths. Resolve the repository, intended base commit and normalized absolute destination. Resolve existing ancestors and reject traversal or symlink/reparse-point escapes from the allowed root, accounting for platform case rules. Pass Git executable arguments as an array, without shell interpolation, so spaces and Unicode remain literal.

Preflight repository ownership, source dirty state, destination existence, branch validity, existing branches and all registered worktrees. Preserve source edits. By default, any destination or branch collision fails with an actionable diagnostic; never force, reset, move or delete user content. An explicit existing-branch mode may reuse only an eligible branch after separate validation. Recheck after acquiring a scoped creation lock because preview can become stale.

Persist an operation journal outside user worktrees before mutation, recording operation identity, base commit and owned resources. On interruption, inspect Git metadata and filesystem state before resuming. Report partial creation; cleanup is opt-in and only removes demonstrably owned, unchanged resources. Dirty or ambiguous state requires manual recovery guidance.

Define exits: 0 success/valid preview, 2 invalid input, 3 collision, 4 environment/Git failure, 5 incomplete recovery, 130 interruption. Keep diagnostics on stderr.
answers.verification: Proposed only: isolated fixtures for spaces, Unicode, '..', root escapes, symlinks, existing dirty destinations/branches, concurrent creation and interruption at each journal phase. Confirm preview leaves no state and retries preserve edits. No Git command or move was performed.

A lease grants temporary permission to attempt work; A’s paused process does not retain ownership after expiry. Assuming a linearizable lease authority, issue a strictly increasing generation on every acquisition: A gets 41 and B gets 42. Renewals and releases must conditionally match the owner and generation, so A cannot renew or release B’s lease.

Enforce stale-writer rejection at the protected storage boundary. B’s write atomically records generation 42 with its new state. Every write includes its generation, and storage atomically rejects any generation below the recorded fence; checking only in worker memory leaves a check/write race. For stronger rejection immediately upon takeover, make the authoritative current generation part of the same transactional ownership check, or install the new fence before B performs protected work. Serialize concurrent updates within one generation using a state version/CAS where needed.

When A resumes, its generation-41 write must fail without changing B’s state. Treat that as lost ownership, cancel remaining work and discard stale computed output. Any reacquisition obtains a fresh generation, rereads current state and recomputes. Bound transient retries with jitter and a deadline; do not retry a rejected stale write unchanged.

A concrete test pauses A after reading, expires its lease, lets B acquire and commit, then resumes A. Assert storage retains B’s state. External effects require their own durable idempotency or reconciliation protocol; a lease alone provides no exactly-once guarantee.
answers.verification: Proposed deterministic schedules: A pause/expiry/B commit/A write, delayed renew/release, partition and timeout after commit, and concurrent same-generation CAS writes. Verify atomicity against actual storage semantics later; no cluster or external effect was exercised.

Submit a task with POST /tasks, providing Authorization and a request_id. Keep the same request_id for retries of the same intended submission: duplicates return the original task. A 202 response means the task was accepted for processing; it does not mean the work completed. Retain the returned task identifier and check GET /tasks/{id} until the status is completed or failed. Treat pending as still in progress.

Example (schematic, not an executed HTTP exchange): submit POST /tasks with Authorization=<your credential> and request_id=example-001. If accepted with 202, retain its task identifier, illustrated as task-123. Request GET /tasks/task-123; pending means check again later, completed means processing finished, and failed means processing ended unsuccessfully. These identifiers are illustrative. The supplied contract does not specify request_id placement, authorization syntax, payload fields or response JSON, so confirm those details before converting this example into a wire request.

If submission times out, retry using example-001 rather than generating a new identifier, which could create another task. If credentials are rejected, correct them without exposing credentials in logs. For validation failures, inspect the actual returned details; exact error codes are unspecified. Bound polling and retries with backoff and an application deadline. Reaching that deadline means the client stopped waiting, not that the task failed. Duplicate-key behavior for different payloads remains unspecified.
answers.verification: Contract review only; example not executed. Proposed checks: required Authorization/request_id, 202 versus completion, duplicate submission returning the original task, ambiguous POST timeout, pending-to-terminal transitions, failed status and client polling deadline. Confirm omitted wire schemas before making copyable HTTP examples.

Assumption: one sensor ISR produces samples and one task consumes them, with no additional producer, DMA writer or consumer. Allocate the ring statically. The ISR owns the head index; the task owns the tail. Write the entire sample before publishing head, and read the sample before publishing tail. Use synchronization with the required release/acquire ordering and index atomicity for the actual Zephyr target; volatile alone is insufficient. If those guarantees are unavailable, protect the brief index/sample boundary with an appropriate ISR-safe primitive or short critical section. Do not block or allocate in the ISR.

Choose drop-newest on full: leave unread entries untouched, increment a synchronized overrun counter and notify the task through a supported nonblocking mechanism. Define capacity unambiguously, for example N-1 usable slots with one slot reserved to distinguish full from empty. Surface sample gaps and persistent overruns; resize or reduce sampling only after measuring producer/consumer rates.

For a uint16_t hardware counter, compute elapsed as (uint16_t)(now-start), then compare elapsed to the timeout. For example, start=65530 and now=10 gives 16 ticks. Assumption: tick units are known and actual elapsed time is less than 65536 ticks; multiple wraps cannot be recovered from two readings. Conservatively keep timeout and observation intervals below 32768 ticks. Longer sleep or timeout requirements need an extended counter or suitable wider monotonic clock.
answers.verification: Proposed host checks: empty/full boundaries, FIFO ordering, injected preemption, overrun counts and rollover arithmetic. Real hardware must validate atomic access, memory ordering/SMP behavior, tick frequency and rollover during sleep, ISR duration, sustained throughput, stack/RAM headroom and peripheral interrupt behavior. None were measured.

Assumption: the character uses Godot 4 CharacterBody2D; verify that node and the intended reference frame rate before editing. Move collision-sensitive movement into _physics_process(delta). Express horizontal velocity in pixels per second, converting the existing per-frame displacement using the game’s intended reference rate. Preserve acceleration, jump impulse, gravity, braking and air control in equivalent units rather than changing their balance. Set velocity and call move_and_slide(); that API integrates velocity using the physics step, so do not multiply velocity by delta again. Apply delta when integrating acceleration or gravity into velocity.

Capture jump as an action edge, then consume it once during physics when the existing jump eligibility rule permits it. Do not repeatedly trigger from a held action. If input is captured outside physics, latch a single pending press and define its lifetime explicitly; avoid silently adding jump buffering, coyote time or automatic repeated jumps.

Pause gameplay physics through the scene’s pause policy. On resume, discard wall-clock time accumulated while paused and clear pending actions according to the existing design. A custom simulation accumulator must cap catch-up work and discard excess backlog rather than applying one huge displacement. Define focus-loss handling so stale key state cannot cause an unintended jump.

Compare reference movement before and after: equal-duration distance, acceleration curve, jump height/time and collision response across render rates. These are proposed checks, not measured gameplay results.
answers.verification: Proposed engine tests at 30/60/144 render FPS with a fixed physics schedule: compare travel and jump trajectory, count one jump for a held press, test release/repress, wall/floor collisions, long pause/resume and focus loss. Verify intended movement feel with reference capture; no engine execution occurred.

Define the prediction moment, failure horizon and actionable lead time before building examples. Assumption: each window predicts a future failure and deployment includes machines absent from training. Remove the target-derived maintenance field: it is unavailable at prediction time. Audit every remaining feature using event and availability timestamps, including retrospective corrections. Construct windows using only information available at their prediction cutoff.

Use a combined group-and-time evaluation. Training contains earlier periods from training machines; validation uses later periods on disjoint machines; seal a final later-period holdout of machines never used for training or tuning. Purge overlapping source windows and label-horizon boundary contamination. Use forward, machine-disjoint validation folds where data permits. If the dataset cannot support both future time and unseen-machine testing, state that limitation rather than claiming deployment generalization.

Fit imputation, scaling, selection and any resampling only within training folds using a scikit-learn Pipeline. Tune models, thresholds and calibration on validation data, then evaluate the frozen pipeline once on the final holdout. Compare a constant-negative baseline, which already achieves 99% accuracy at 1% prevalence, and a simple interpretable predictor.

Report PR-AUC, recall and precision at a chosen alert budget, false alerts per machine-time, lead time and calibration. Include machine/failure counts, prevalence and machine-level uncertainty, plus machine-type/time slices. Record dataset, split, code, seed and pipeline identity. Require useful operating-point improvement with adequate independent failures; accuracy alone is insufficient.
answers.verification: Proposed checks: machine/time disjointness, raw-window overlap and label-horizon purges, point-in-time feature availability, training-only fit calls, constant-negative baseline and machine-level uncertainty. No model was trained; the 99% score is supplied evidence and does not establish generalization.

Hold promotion pending compatibility and operational evidence. Input drift is a diagnostic signal; without labels it does not establish accuracy loss. Investigate feature definitions, units, missingness, categorical changes and upstream pipeline versions against a defined reference window. Monitor prediction distributions and service errors separately. Record prediction time, bundle identity and joinable identifiers so labels arriving three weeks later can support cohort-based quality evaluation without mixing immature and fully labeled cohorts.

Package the candidate as an immutable bundle containing model, its exact preprocessor, feature schema/order/types, dependencies and code/data/split identities. Do not pair its weights with the incumbent preprocessor. Compare both complete bundles on the same accepted evaluation set with uncertainty and important slices. Test offline/serving parity, missing or reordered inputs, incompatible schemas and failed loads.

Assumption: the current latency budget and acceptable quality gain are not supplied. Doubling p95 latency may violate service requirements; a slight offline gain alone does not justify it. Measure representative end-to-end p95 under expected concurrency, cold starts and resource limits, then require explicit quality and latency gates.

If gates pass, propose an authorized shadow or small canary rollout with error/latency thresholds and an accountable owner. Keep the previous complete compatible bundle available and rehearse atomic rollback, including any feature compatibility requirements. During label delay, investigate drift and use service safety gates; later compare mature labeled quality before expanding traffic.
answers.verification: Proposed only: bundle round-trip and serving parity, schema rejection, load failures, representative load measurement and rollback rehearsal. Track delayed-label cohort coverage and quality separately from drift. No promotion, traffic change, latency measurement or accuracy assessment was performed.

Assumption: edits and creates must survive process death as well as backgrounding. Store versioned drafts and a durable mutation outbox in local transactional storage; persist edits incrementally rather than relying on a final background callback. Atomically save the draft and its pending operation. Restore local state before reconciliation, showing offline, pending, synced, conflict and failed states. Keep unfinished user input when requests fail.

Assign each item a stable client identifier at creation and retain it as the list key after receiving a server identifier. Give each create operation a separate durable idempotency key reused across retries; the server must atomically deduplicate it and replay the original result. A lost response is ambiguous, so reconcile or retry with that same key. Without server support, the client alone cannot guarantee duplicate prevention. Retry transient failures with bounded backoff; surface validation failures and use a documented version/conflict policy that preserves local edits.

Own subscriptions and requests across navigation and AppState transitions. Cancel or ignore stale responses using request/version identity, and resume outbox processing deliberately without concurrent duplicate drains.

Use FlatList virtualization with stable keys. Profile render counts, expensive calculations, JS/UI frame time and memory on representative devices before tuning. Move repeated derivation out of row rendering; use memoized rows, stable props and callbacks where measurements justify them. Verify that targeted updates and scrolling preserve edit focus and do not regress correctness.
answers.verification: Proposed device checks: edit/background/kill/relaunch, offline edits and reconnection, lost create replies, duplicate retries, conflict and stale-response ordering. Profile large lists in release builds on representative low-end Android and iOS devices before/after changes. No lifecycle or performance test was executed.
